summary: Kanchu Onoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He taught at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and was a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his doctorate under Yün-hua Jan, later holding an appointment at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).
Kang-yuan Sung is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Calgary under supervisor Anthony W. Barber and studied under Anne Moore and Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris, later serving in a嘱託 (shokutaku) post at Tokyo National Museum.

Kanji Tamura (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies. His career includes appointments at Rissho University as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).

Kanoko Tanaka specializes in religious studies and Indology. She studied under the traditional teacher Acharya Tulsi and held an appointment as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962). He also served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).
Kanti Chandra Pandey (1903–1971) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who founded the University of Lucknow and held an academic post there (attested 1950).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned degrees from Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu universities. She founded the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, serving as academic director and chairperson.

Karam Tej Singh Sarao (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin and K. R. Norman, and became a professor at the University of Delhi in 1995.

Karandagolle Sobhitha specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. After earning an MPhil from the University of Peradeniya, where he served as a temporary lecturer (2011–2015), he was Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka (2015–2021).

Karel Glaser (1845–1913) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Vienna, completing a PhD under Georg Bühler, and taught at the Stadtgymnasium Trieste from 1880 to 1900.

Karel Oštir (1888–1973) was an Indo-European linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Vienna under Paul Kretschmer and earned his PhD at the University of Graz under Rudolf Meringer, later serving as professor at the University of Ljubljana.
Karel Přikryl (1718–1785) was an Indologist and linguist. He taught at Rachol Seminary from circa 1754 to 1761 and served as Rector of the Jesuit College in Hradec Králové in 1768.

Karel Werner (1925–2019) was an Indologist and philosopher. Educated at Palacký University Olomouc, he taught Indian philosophy at Durham University (1969–1990) and later held professorial posts at Masaryk University and SOAS University of London.

Karen Christina Lang works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her doctorate at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, also studying at Banaras Hindu University, and served as a professor at the University of Virginia.
Karen Katsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She has held posts as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 2006) and at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a scholar of religious studies. She studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University, and served as a professor of anthropology at Drew University from circa 1976 to 2009.

Karen Nelson Villanueva is a religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies and studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero has held academic posts at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago, and she taught Sally McAra.
